title: Symmetry: Lines of Symmetry and Rotational Symmetry
seo_title: Symmetry Class 6 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Line of symmetry (reflection symmetry) and rotational symmetry, order and angle of rotational symmetry of figures (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 6)
meta_desc: Class 6 Symmetry worksheet (Ganita Prakash Chapter 9): lines of symmetry of shapes and letters, order and angle of rotational symmetry. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry
body_html:
How it works

A line of symmetry divides a figure into two mirror halves. A rectangle has 2 (not along its diagonals); a square has 4; a regular n-sided polygon has n.

A figure has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a turn of less than 360°. The order is how many times it fits onto itself in a full turn; the angle of symmetry is 360° ÷ order.

Example

What is the angle of symmetry of a regular hexagon?

Order 6

360° ÷ 6

Answer: 60°

Example

How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?

Through the mid-points of opposite sides

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

  • Counting the diagonals of a rectangle as lines of symmetry.
  • Saying a shape with no rotational symmetry has order 0 (it has order 1).
  • Multiplying instead of dividing 360° by the order.

faq.q: What is a line of symmetry?
faq.a: A line that divides a figure into two parts that are mirror images of each other.

faq.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry?
faq.a: The number of times a figure looks the same during one full turn.

faq.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
faq.a: Infinitely many — every diameter is a line of symmetry.
